slides.title: Alibaba Qoder - An Agentic Coding Alibaba Qoder
slides.text: Alibaba Qoder - An Agentic Coding Alibaba Qoder - An Agentic Coding Platform Editor, advanced context engineering, hybrid retrieval architectures ( combining code graphs and vector search ), long-term memory systems, and spec-driven workflows Two primary modes: Agent & Quest Agent Mode - coding assistant , conversational pair programming Quest Mode - fully autonomous coding specialist. Plans, implements, tests, and verifies code, outputting production-ready solutions Deep repo searching and automated documentation generation with a "Repo Wiki" Automated Refactoring & Testing Qoder automatically selects optimal AI models for each task (Claude, Gemini, and GPT, ...) MCP (Memory, Context, Plugins) , compatibility with external tools, web search, auto-run terminal commands, and broad language coverage Uses Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B-Instruct Limitations: Does not currently support Linux (but works with MacOS and Windows); Repo Wiki and auto-indexing have scale limits; Some developer plugins (e.g., GitHub Pull Requests) currently suffer version compatibility issues Qoder is completely free to use with no rate limits Download and install the IDE from https://qoder.com

slides.text: NVIDIA's Nemotron Nano 2 NVIDIA's Nemotron Nano 2 Mamba-Transformer hybrid Most self-attention layers replaced with Mamba-2 layers The architecture uses just 6 attention layers alongside 28 Mamba-2 layers and 28 FFN layers Up to 6x faster A 9B parameter model that runs 128K context on a single A10G GPU (just 22GB memory) The model was trained on 20 trillion tokens, then compressed from 12B to 9B parameters while maintaining performance. Importance: High-quality reasoning models can run on single GPUs instead of clusters https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.14444 - paper

slides.title: AI Updates - 1 Memory Decoder: A Pretrained,
slides.text: AI Updates - 1 Memory Decoder: A Pretrained, Plug-and-Play LLM Memory https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.09874 Memory Decoder is a small (0.5B-1B) model that learns to mimic retrieval (RAG) behavior through specialized pretraining During inference, it runs in parallel with the main LLM, with outputs interpolated together A Memory Decoder works with any model sharing the same tokenizer - true plug-and-play domain adaptation Research shows that a single 0.5B Memory Decoder reduces domain-specific perplexity by 76-79% in biomedicine and finance. Inference overhead is just 1.28x compared to RAG's 2.17x Remarkably, a 0.5B model with Memory Decoder outperforms vanilla 72B models - that's 140x parameter efficiency Apple Explores Google Gemini for Siri. Also considers OpenAI and Anthropic. GitHub has open-sourced its own MCP server It allows LLMs to interface with GitHub reducing hallucinations and unlocking new automation workflows https://github.blog/open-source/maintainers/why-we-open-sourced-our-mcp-server-and-what-it-means-for-you/ OpenAI Assistants API => Responses API : code interpreter, persistent conversations, MCP, and computer use; web search gets domain filtering, source reporting, and a price cut from $25 to $10/1K calls

slides.title: Build Your Own $80M Website Builder Build Your
slides.text: Build Your Own $80M Website Builder Build Your Own $80M Website Builder in Under 1 Hour (with Claude Code) - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZBBzTs0Ow7E Anand, a former Flexport engineer and founder, demonstrates building the core features of Base44 - an app sold for $80 million six months after launch - using Claude Code in under an hour App includes a full-stack website and SaaS builder, offering instant database, authentication, and payments Start with wireframing in Excalidraw, then detailed planning using advanced AI models (initially GPT-5), resulting in thorough task breakdowns before code generation Step-by-Step Workflow - Wireframing & Planning: Initial UI/UX is mapped out in Excalidraw; screenshots and descriptive prompts are sent to AI to generate a precise implementation checklist Planning Document: Tasks are grouped into epics (large milestones), with a checklist for each. These cover everything from layout to backend features; Cloud Code IDE: Anand uses Claude Code (sometimes inside Cursor IDE) to automatically scaffold the project, leveraging planning mode to review and approve steps before execution. The Claude Code automates folder structure, setup, and Next.js integration Custom Commands & Subagents: The video explains the difference - commands are reusable system prompts, while subagents parallelize workflows across tasks or codebase sections. Subagents are particularly useful for large-scale collaborative projects or batch operations Rapid creation of a three-pane layout: chat on the left, folder navigator center, live website preview right (all controlled via AI) Integration with Monaco editor for in-browser code editing, autosave functionality, and keyboard shortcuts Project persistence, planning document updates, and automated git commits after tasks complete for robust tracking Use of Sandpack for in-browser code previews; various advanced commands for code analysis and documentation Key Insights and Tips: Cloud Code Planning Mode: Review and approve proposed changes before code is generated Effective Task Management: Maintain separate planning and to-do files to persist context and project history across sessions Parallelism with Subagents: Divide labor across multiple agents for design updates or feature rollouts, preventing bottlenecks in complex codebases Critique and Refinement: Harness multiple AI models for critiquing and iterating on plans, ensuring completeness and relevant feature prioritization

slides.title: Stacking Sliding Windows Problem Why Stacking Sliding Windows
slides.text: Stacking Sliding Windows Problem Why Stacking Sliding Windows Can't See Very Far Modern LLMs use sliding window attention to handle long texts efficiently. These models struggle to use information from more than about 1,500 words ago, far less than the theoretical 100,000. This is because information gets diluted as it spreads through the network, and residual connections create an exponential barrier that blocks distant information. https://guangxuanx.com/blog/stacking-swa.html

slides.title: Memento: Finetuning Agents Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without
slides.text: Memento: Finetuning Agents Memento: Fine-tuning LLM Agents without Fine-tuning LLMs A memory-based, continual-learning framework that helps LLM agents improve from experience without updating model weights https://github.com/Agent-on-the-Fly/Memento Core Concept - Learn from experiences, not gradients. Memento logs successful & failed trajectories into a Case Bank and retrieves by value to steer planning and execution, enabling low-cost, transferable, and online continual learning No LLM weight updates. Memento reframes continual learning as memory-based online reinforcement learning over a memory-augmented MDP. A neural case-selection policy guides actions; experiences are stored and reused via efficient Read/Write operations Two-stage planner–executor loop. A CBR-driven Planner decomposes tasks and retrieves relevant cases; an Executor runs each subtask as an MCP client, orchestrating tools and writing back outcomes Comprehensive tool ecosystem. Built-in support for web search, document processing, code execution, image/video analysis, and more through a unified MCP interface Strong benchmark performance. Achieves competitive results across GAIA, DeepResearcher, SimpleQA, and HLE benchmarks

slides.title: FastAPI Example from fastapi import FastAPI from pydantic
slides.text: FastAPI Example from fastapi import FastAPI from pydantic import BaseModel from typing import Optional app = FastAPI() # ---------------------------------- # Pydantic Models class UserRequest(BaseModel): name: str age: Optional[int] = None email: Optional[str] = None is_active: Optional[bool] = True score: Optional[float] = None class UserResponse(BaseModel): id: int name: str age: Optional[int] = None email: Optional[str] = None is_active: bool score: Optional[float] = None message: str # ---------------------------------- # In-memory storage users = [] user_counter = 1 # --------------------------------------------- # GET endpoint @app.get("/users/{user_id}", response_model=UserResponse) async def get_user(user_id: int): user = next((u for u in users if u["id"] == user_id), None) if user: return UserResponse(**user, message=" User found ") return UserResponse( id=user_id, name="Unknown", is_active=False, message="User not found" ) # --------------------------------------------- # POST endpoint @app.post("/users", response_model=UserResponse) async def create_user(user: UserRequest): global user_counter new_user = { "id": user_counter, "name": user.name, "age": user.age, "email": user.email, "is_active": user.is_active, "score": user.score } users.append(new_user) user_counter += 1 return UserResponse(**new_user, message=" User created successfully ") # Run with: uvicorn main:app --reload # test with https://localhost:8000/docs

slides.title: Deep Think with Confidence DeepConf - new method
slides.text: Deep Think with Confidence DeepConf - new method from Meta for improving LLM reasoning DeepConf = Deep Think with Confidence https://jiaweizzhao.github.io/deepconf/ https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.15260 https://jiaweizzhao.github.io/deepconf/static/pdfs/deepconf_arxiv.pdf - paper DeepConf uses internal confidence scores to filter out low-quality reasoning traces Achieves higher accuracy and greatly reduced computation Outperforms standard majority voting on complex benchmarks while requiring up to 84.7% fewer generated tokens DeepConf is simple to implement DeepConf does not need extra training or tuning How the Confidence Scores Are Constructed: Token Confidence - based on the negative average log-probability of the top-k token predictions (higher log-probability means higher confidence). Group Confidence - the model averages confidence scores over sliding windows (short ranges of steps) to capture local trends, rather than just a global, sequence-wide metric. Tail Confidence - emphasizes the confidence of the last part of the reasoning trace, since final answers often reveal reasoning errors missed earlier. Lowest Group Confidence - the weakest segment of the trace. A  sudden drop in confidence is highly predictive of an error or reasoning collapse. Bottom Percentile Confidence - the bottom x% of token confidence values within a trace to surface the most error-prone parts. Early Filtering - DeepConf can discard low-confidence paths before they reach completion or enter voting, saving computation and focusing on high-quality traces only. By capturing local uncertainty, DeepConf can stop poor traces early, avoiding "averaging out" errors or letting low-quality reasoning dilute the answer. Weighted Voting: Instead of treating all traces equally when voting, DeepConf assigns higher voting weight to traces with higher confidence, making it more robust to noisy, ambiguous, or error-prone traces. DeepConf often achieves equal or better accuracy than majority voting with up to 85% fewer generated tokens.
